subject: Urgent: customer-facing retry flood causing 5xx/429 spike (BrightRoute)
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightroute.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightRoute SRE <sre@brightroute.com>, Helen Yang <helen.yang@brightroute.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: sudden spike in 5xx/429 during peak routing window

Vivek / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from your API between 07:45 and 08:15 PST during our morning batch. Throughput dropped and our scheduler retried aggressively which made the situation worse on our end. Attached is a trimmed log with request timestamps and status codes (brightroute_error_sample.log).

This is impacting our SLAs for late shipments — we need immediate attention. Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side incident or if we have a bad client-side retry loop?

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Head of Integrations, BrightRoute

BrightRoute Logistics

Sam — thanks for the log. We’re on it. Quick summary of what I’ve done: I looped in Marissa (SRE lead) and Stephanie (SDK PM) to triage. Initial telemetry shows elevated 429s across the us-west region coincident with your traffic spike. We’re collecting traces and will escalate if this looks like a platform overload.

We also noticed your logs show many retries at ~200ms intervals which can amplify error load. Can you share the client SDK config you’re using (retry/backoff settings)? Attaching a link for a fast triage doc.

- Vivek

Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden spike in 5xx/429 during peak routing window

Vivek — I pulled the prod request histogram and error traces. Key findings so far:
- Region: us-west1, elevated error rate started 07:42 PST and peaked at 07:54 PST.
- Primary error: 429 rate went from baseline 0.3% to 12% during the spike; 5xxs (502/503) rose concurrently.
- Backpressure signals present on some serving nodes (queue depth and concurrent token limits hit).

Crucial observation: several client IPs show retry patterns with near-constant intervals (~150-350ms) with no backoff multiplier. That aligns with BrightRoute’s log snippet. When many clients do this, it converges into a retry flood that pushes nodes into transient overload and produces 5xx churn.

Next steps proposed:
1) Short-term: we can temporarily enable stricter rate-limits for the account and route their traffic to a protected capacity pool while we stabilize.
2) Medium-term: ask BrightRoute to update SDK retry settings to exponential backoff and jitter (we have a recommended config).
3) Stephanie to check whether our official SDK shipped a default aggressive retry policy in the last minor release.

I’ll continue collecting full traces and a bundle for postmortem.

— Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Runtime

On Wed, Feb 10, 2027 at 08:37 AM vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the log. We’re on it...
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden spike in 5xx/429 during peak routing window

Folks — I pulled the SDK change log. We shipped an update (v1.6.2) that relaxed default retry spacing for low-latency hopefulness — it starts at 100ms with a linear increment of +100ms up to 3 retries. That config is plainly too aggressive under load and lacks jitter.

I’m preparing a hotfix to flip the default to exponential backoff with randomized jitter and a higher initial delay. I can also push a warning to customers on the SDK changelog and a one-click config snippet to opt into safe defaults.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Marissa: enable protected routing for BrightRoute for the next 2 hours.
- Vivek: ask BrightRoute to apply the attached sdk-config.json (recommended backoff) for a quick mitigation.
- Rishi: we may need an exec note given revenue impact and possible SLA credit.

Stephanie Nguyen
Product Manager, SDKs
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden spike in 5xx/429 during peak routing window

Sam / Helen — quick update and immediate request:

What we found: partial platform backpressure combined with your client retry behavior (default SDK settings with short linear retries) created a feedback loop — effectively a retry flood. This is a client-amplified incident, but we will both mitigate and remediate.

Immediate actions completed:
- We routed your traffic to a protected capacity pool and throttled aggressive clients at the edge (should reduce 5xx/429 within ~10–15 minutes).
- Stephanie attached a recommended sdk-config.json (see attachments) that sets exp backoff with jitter; please apply to your fleet ASAP.
- We opened JIRA-INC-7182 for the platform side to ensure autoscaling/queue-shed thresholds are tuned to avoid cascade failures.

Can you schedule a 30-min follow-up at 13:00 PST to validate metrics after they settle? If you can patch one instance to the recommended config we can watch in real time.

Thanks for the quick escalation — we’ll drive to a resolution and follow up with a summary and remediation plan.

— Vivek
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
